newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 50-55 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 50-55 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 50 to 55 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for an overall build ranged from 40 bcf to 70 bcf for the week ended October 18. The four-week average is 76 bcf.
"There was some cold weather in the East, so I don't think we'll see much injection there. We could see a low number," said one Midwest trader.
Last week, AGA showed overall storage gained just 38 bcf, well-below expectations. Stocks were still 261 bcf, or nine percent below the same year-ago period.
Eastern stocks rose to 91 percent of capacity last week, about two points below last year. But producing region inventories at 71 percent full continued to lag 1995 by about 17 percentage points.

Last year at this time, total inventories gained 52 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would leave the gap to 1995 roughly unchanged. For the same week in 1995, eastern storage rose by 29 bcf, while producing stocks were up 18 bcf.
